{{c|{{larger|FIRST EPISTLE OF S. PAVL TO}}}}
{{c|{{larger|THE THESSALONIANS.}}}}

{{dropinitial|H}}OVV S. Paul vvith Silas (or Siluanus) and Timothee according to a vi{{ls}}ion calling him out of A{{ls}}ia into Macedonia, came to Philippi being the fir{{ls}}t citie thereof, vve reade Act. 16. And hovv againe from Philippi, after {{ls}}courging and impri{{ls}}oning there, he came to The{{ls}}{{ls}}alonica being the head citie of that countrie, vve reade Act. 17. vvhere after 3 vveekes preaching, the Ievves {{ls}}tirred the citie again{{ls}}t them, and pur{{ls}}ued them al{{ls}}o to Beraea: {{ls}}o that Paul vvas conueied from thence to Athens, vvhere he expected the cōming of Silas & Timothee from the fore{{ls}}aid Beraea in Macedonia, but receiued them (as vve haue Act. 18.) at Corinth in Achaia.

Hauing therefore left the The{{ls}}{{ls}}alonians in {{ls}}uch per{{ls}}ecution, and being careful to knovv hovv they did in it, he vvas de{{ls}}irous to returne vnto them, as he {{ls}}ignifieth in the 2 chapter of this Epi{{ls}}tle v. 17. But (as he there addeth) ''Satan hindered vs.'' therefore tarying him {{ls}}elf at Athens, he {{ls}}endeth Timothee vnto them, at vvho{{ls}}e returne vnder{{ls}}tanding their con{{ls}}tancie, he is much comforted, as he declareth c. 3. So then they are all three together at the vvriting of this Epi{{ls}}tle, as al{{ls}}o vve haue in the title of it: ''Paul and Siluanus and Timothee to the Church of the The{{ls}}{{ls}}alonians.'' And therefore it {{ls}}eemeth to haue bene vvritten at Corinth, not at Athens: becau{{ls}}e after the {{ls}}ending of Timothee to The{{ls}}{{ls}}alonica, they mette not at Athens againe, but at Corinth.

The fir{{ls}}t three chapters of it are, to confirme and comfort them again{{ls}}t the tentations of tho{{ls}}e per{{ls}}ecutions. The other tvvo are of exhortation, to liue according to his preceptes, namely in {{ls}}anctification of their bodies, and not in fornication: to loue one an other: to comfort one an other about their frendes departed, vvith the doctrine of the Re{{ls}}urrection, and vvith continuall preparation to die: the laietie to obey, and the Cleargie to be diligent in euery point of their office.<noinclude>{{continues|THE}}
